attributes.residual:
BEST RETAINED: UNCHANGED at real 628, insns T857/O855, multiset 6t. No source change kept in this function.

MECHANISM D3, NOW CORRECTLY NAMED - and v2's framing of it was incomplete. v2 read the hoist as SLOT THEFT ('consuming slot 144, neededPct's home') and inferred that killing it would hand D3 the target's slot map. The aligned view says the slot is the lesser half of the damage. The target computes the checksum loop bound AT the loop as a single RECORDING instruction:
    938: lwz r4,180(r1)          <- reload bigSize from its declaration-order home
    940: addic. r0,r4,-23992     <- subtract AND set CR0 in one instruction
    944: li r4,0
    94c: mtctr r0
    958: beq ->96c               <- zero-trip guard, consuming the CR0 that addic. set
One instruction feeds BOTH the CTR count and the zero-trip branch. Under D3, MWCC hoists `bigSize - 23992` to the prologue as `lwz r3,172(r1); addi r0,r3,-23992; stw r0,144(r1)`, which SPLITS that fused `addic.` into a plain `addi` (now far away, in the prologue) plus a separate `cmpwi`/`cmplwi` left behind at the loop. That is the exact content of D3's multiset delta `target-only +1 addic. / ours-only -1 addi -1 cmpwi`. So the hoist costs a fused instruction, not merely a frame slot, and the `volatile` on bigSize in the RETAINED baseline is what forbids the hoist and therefore what preserves the fusion.

This makes MECHANISM D a genuine two-sided trade rather than a one-sided defect, which is why every de-volatile probe to date has been negative: `volatile` buys the addic. fusion and the memory home, and costs the volatile-sub-block segregation (36 instructions carrying a wrong (r1) displacement, ~72 of the 628 real). D3 pays the fusion to buy the slot map back. Both directions have now been measured and the volatile side is worth more.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY CLOSE IT (for the next lane, but NOT as a cheap probe - all three cheap ones are spent): a form that is memory-homed in DECLARATION order, not loop-invariant-hoistable, and not volatile-segregated. `volatile` gives the first two and forces the third; the plain form gives neither of the first two. v2's D2 established that an aggregate is memory-homed WITHOUT volatile but MWCC scalarizes it into allocator order, so the aggregate route needs the scalarization blocked, not the homing.

DO-NOT-RETRY on this function: de-volatile of the four wide locals (v2 probe 4, real 910); de-volatile of all five (D3a, 754); all five plus definition sink (D3b, 754); all five plus scoped opt_lifetimes off (D3c, 944); four plus opt_lifetimes off (v2 D1, 962); the reversed-member aggregate (v2 D2, 914); scoped peephole off (v1, 1096); opt_dead_code off (v1, neutral-identical, compiler does not honour it).
